title: Discovery and interrogatories - civil procedure tools lawyers forget
p1:
Many lawyers spend hours preparing for trial, but overlook two tools that can shape the entire case before they enter the courtroom.

Discovery and interrogatories are often the quiet weapons of civil procedure.
p2:
A common misconception is that discovery is just a paperwork exchange. In reality, it is a way to uncover facts, test the opposing side’s story, and narrow the issues before trial.

Interrogatories are written questions that require formal answers under oath. The surprising part? A well-crafted interrogatory can reveal a timeline, identify key witnesses, or expose gaps in an opponent’s position.
p3:
Used strategically, these tools save time and prevent courtroom surprises. The goal is not to ask more questions, but to ask the questions that force clarity.

A practical takeaway: the strongest discovery requests are built around the facts you need to prove, not just the documents you hope to collect.
